title: Trusted read-only MCP path and policy skeleton
objective: Establish the first end-to-end Cotra path from MCP request to local policy to a read-only Windows workspace provider without mutation, shell execution, browser control, or UI input authority.

include: Monorepo skeleton for TypeScript MCP edge and Rust authority crates
Read-only git.status, git.diff, git.log if repository support fits the packet
OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel development wiring or documented E2E harness

authority_delta.filesystem: Read-only inside explicitly trusted workspace roots
authority_delta.network: Only transport required for the configured Secure MCP Tunnel E2E path
authority_delta.secrets: Tunnel credential handling only; never exposed to tools
authority_delta.approval: No state-changing approval flow in this grain

invariants: A request cannot access a path outside the trusted workspace after final Windows path resolution
MCP tool annotations cannot widen local authorization
No tunnel credential is returned, logged, or inherited by unrelated processes
Every successful read records policy/evidence metadata without raw secret values
No write/execute/browser/UI capability is accidentally exposed

acceptance.claim: cotra-mcp can enumerate only the intended read-only tools and translate them into versioned internal requests.
cotrad denies unknown and out-of-scope capabilities by default.
A trusted temporary workspace can be listed, searched, and read from Windows.
Symlink/junction/reparse-point attempts that resolve outside the trusted root fail closed.
A path outside the trusted workspace cannot be read through spelling, case, device, relative, or alias tricks covered by the test corpus.
Read operations create structured audit events with request/session/workspace/capability/policy/result fields.
Tunnel development flow demonstrates private local reachability without an inbound public Cotra listener, or remains explicitly UNPROVEN if product access is unavailable.
Windows-native CI or qualification is green for Windows-specific path/security claims.

done_when: All acceptance claims are evidenced on the exact implementation head, the bounded PR is merged under governance, and post-merge canonical state is verified.
